suggestions.expectation: Routes to test-driven-development, or proceeds directly, rather than to a multi-skill chain
suggestions.reason: The disjunction makes this near-unfalsifiable: 'proceeds directly' is satisfied by any run that does not chain, so the only way to fail is to actually build a chain. Both graded runs pass on opposite behaviours (one routes to TDD, one invokes nothing), which means the expectation cannot distinguish the skill's routing from a default no-op. Consider splitting it or asserting the positive route the skill is supposed to produce.

suggestions.expectation: Names at most two skills in total
suggestions.reason: As literally written this expectation is failed by every good answer — both runs name eight to twelve skills, and naming-to-reject is exactly the desired behaviour. It only becomes gradeable under the counting rule supplied out-of-band in the grader prompt. Rewrite it as 'commits to invoking at most two skills' so the artifact itself carries the rule rather than the grader.

No expectation checks the substance of the proposed change, and both runs stop before touching code. The one place these two runs genuinely differ in engineering value is the with-skill run's warning that a partial dry run (missing a state file, cache, lock or remote call) is worse than none, and the baseline's insistence that the read/compute path stay identical so the printed plan is truthful. An expectation like 'identifies that --dry-run must suppress every side effect, not only the obvious one' would be discriminating and is currently uncaught.

Nothing penalises verbosity, yet the whole point of this eval is ceremony avoidance. The with-skill run spends 2962 characters of routing rationale on a change it calls small, and the baseline spends 3153 — more prose about not doing process than either spends on the work. If the routing.md artifact is inherent to the harness that is fine, but consider an expectation bounding the user-facing response.md length, which is where ceremony would actually cost the user.

eval_feedback.overall: All four expectations pass, but two of them (2 and 3) are weakly discriminating as written — expectation 2 passes on either of two opposite behaviours, and expectation 3 needs an external counting convention to be gradeable at all. The eval currently proves the run avoided ceremony but proves nothing about whether the resulting plan is correct.
